guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 authorization code flows for REST API access on behalf of a user. The narrowest documented scope that covers listing issues over REST is read_api, which is broad: read access to all groups and projects the connected user can reach. Issue listing returns only issues the authenticated user can access, and pagination is documented. Registration, redirect setup and token exchange remain untested setup requirements.

steps.title: Register a user-owned GitLab OAuth application with redirect URI and read_api scope
steps.detail: Developer creates an OAuth application in GitLab (user-owned via Edit profile > Access > Applications, or group-owned via group Settings > Applications) with the redirect URI for the integration and the read_api scope. GitLab then provides the Application ID (client ID) and Client Secret. This is the documented prerequisite for authorization code flow; the test cannot run until it is done.
steps.doneWhen: An application exists with a redirect URI and read_api scope, and its Application ID and Client Secret are stored securely for testing.

steps.title: List issues in a project the connected person can access and read the title field
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v4/projects/:id/issues with the user's OAuth bearer token. Each element of the returned array exposes title as $[].title (string). Identify the project by its id or URL-encoded full path (for example group%2Fproject) that the user provided. Pagination is page/per_page with a Link header; this first call requests page 1.
steps.doneWhen: Response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array; each item has a title string; the Link header is inspected for rel="next". Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
